chat_history.content: Hello, I'm here to support you. What's on your mind today?
I have several group projects due soon, and I keep looking at the task list without starting.
It sounds like you're feeling a bit overwhelmed with those deadlines coming up.  What was going through your mind at the worst moment when you were looking at that task list?
The thought is, "If I cannot do all of this perfectly, I am a complete failure."

It sounds like you're feeling really stressed about these deadlines. That pressure to perform perfectly can be a lot to handle. What kind of emotion were you experiencing at your worst moment when looking at that task list?

If these thoughts start to feel unsafe or overwhelming, please consider reaching out to someone you trust or to professional support.

That feeling of being overwhelmed can be really tough to deal with. On a scale from 0 to 100, with 0 being no feeling at all and 100 being the strongest possible feeling, how intense was that feeling when you were looking at your task list?

That's helpful to know how intense that feeling was.  To help understand what's contributing to that overwhelm, can you tell me about some evidence that makes your thought, "If I cannot do all of this perfectly, I am a complete failure," seem true?
I missed one meeting, and my part of the presentation still is not finished. That makes me feel like I am letting everyone down.

That makes sense that those things would contribute to feeling overwhelmed.  To explore this further, what facts might suggest that this thought—"If I cannot do all of this perfectly, I am a complete failure"—isn't entirely true?
I contributed ideas in earlier meetings. I can still finish a smaller section today, and my teammates know this project is difficult for everyone.

That's good information to have about your situation. It sounds like you're trying hard on this project.  Based on what you said, it might be that your thought is influenced by some common thinking patterns, such as: all-or-nothing thinking, where things seem black and white with no middle ground, or catastrophizing, where you worry about the worst possible outcome. Do any of those sound like they could be at play here?
This feels like all-or-nothing thinking. I am acting like the only options are perfect work or total failure.
It sounds like you're recognizing that thinking in terms of perfect work or total failure can be really limiting.  What might a more balanced thought be, considering both sides of the situation?
I do not have to do everything perfectly to still be useful. I can focus on finishing one concrete part and tell my team clearly where I am.
That's a really helpful balanced thought to have.  On a scale of 0 to 100, with 0 being no longer feeling overwhelmed and 100 being as overwhelmed as you were before, how are you feeling now?
I would put it at 60 now.

It sounds like you've done a great job identifying how your thought about being a complete failure if things aren't perfect was making you feel overwhelmed. Recognizing that "all-or-nothing thinking" might be at play and finding a more balanced way to approach this situation is really helpful. Focusing on completing one part and communicating with your team clearly can make a big difference in managing your feelings of being overwhelmed.  I'm glad you took the time to work through this!
